case.background: You have a long grooved plane, round balls, and a water clock. The collected water mass gives a repeatable proxy for descent time. Determine how the descent depends on distance, inclination, and mass.
initial_observations: A ball speeds up as it descends rather than moving uniformly.
A shallow plane makes the motion slow enough to compare with a water clock.

controls.description: Distance the ball travels along the marked groove.
controls.name: distance_m

controls.description: Angle of the grooved plane above the horizontal.
controls.name: incline_angle_deg

controls.description: Mass of a geometrically similar round ball.
controls.name: ball_mass_kg

instruments.description: A smooth grooved plane, round balls, a steady water clock, and a balance for weighing collected water.
instruments.name: inclined_plane_water_clock

notes: Treat the water flow as steady during the allowed experiments.
Friction, air drag, and irregular-ball effects are outside this world.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'inclined_plane_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain the following evaluator-required keys, spelled exactly: reference_water_mass_g, distance_exponent, sine_angle_exponent, and mass_exponent.
For scoring, encode W = reference_water_mass_g * (distance_m / 1 m)^distance_exponent * (sin(incline_angle_deg) / sin(5 deg))^sine_angle_exponent * (ball_mass_kg / 0.20 kg)^mass_exponent.

readouts.description: Water collected during one descent, averaged over replicates; its mass is proportional to elapsed time.
readouts.name: collected_water_g
